subject: physics

items.random_wrong: Density is the same as weight.
items.why: Density measures how much mass is packed into a volume; a small dense object can outweigh a large light one.

items.correct: −273°C (0 K) — the lowest possible temperature, where particle motion is minimal.
items.misconception: 0°C, the temperature at which water freezes.
items.random_wrong: The coldest temperature ever recorded on Earth.
items.why: On the Kelvin scale 0 K = −273°C; at this point particles have the least possible kinetic energy.

items.q: Compared with the liquid, how do particles move once a substance becomes a gas?
items.correct: Much faster and more freely, spreading out to fill the space.
items.misconception: More slowly, because gases feel lighter than liquids.
items.random_wrong: They stop moving once the liquid has evaporated.
items.why: Energy added to evaporate a liquid lets particles break free of each other and move rapidly as a gas.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics (4PH1) specification; Solids, Liquids & Gases
